summary: Taiwan waives visas for 65 nationalities — 90 days for the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand among others — and 20 more can apply online for an eVisa. Remaining nationalities apply for a visitor visa at a Taiwan overseas mission.

primarySources.name: Bureau of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Taiwan)

declarations.name: Taiwan Arrival Card
declarations.text: Foreign visitors without an Alien Resident Certificate, resident visa or diplomatic ID must submit the online Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC) on the National Immigration Agency's site within 7 days before arrival. Hong Kong, Macao and mainland travellers holding multiple-entry permits must submit it too.

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Taiwan travel advice, entry requirements
conflict.states: Submit the TWAC within three days before arrival

currencyLimits.text: The UK FCDO says you must declare cash or travellers cheques worth more than NT$100,000 or US$10,000 on arrival.

source.name: UK FCDO — Taiwan travel advice (entry requirements)

notes: Do not bring animal products into Taiwan without authorisation: the UK FCDO says you may face a heavy fine, and customs have increased inspections because of African swine fever in pork products.

Taiwan Customs allows travellers aged 18 or over 1.5 litres of alcohol duty-free, and those aged 20 or over 200 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 1 lb of smoking tobacco. E-cigarettes, e-liquid and heated tobacco products not approved by the Ministry of Health and Welfare are prohibited.

Taiwan Customs says inbound passengers may not bring in any fruit: quarantine officers confiscate and destroy it, and the passenger is fined NT$3,000 or more. Almost all animals, plants and their products are prohibited unless a quarantine certificate is presented.

payments.text: No official source we read describes card acceptance or ATMs in Taiwan.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says crime rates are extremely low in Taiwan, and the Government of Canada says violent crime is rare but petty crime such as pickpocketing occurs. Both say typhoons usually occur between May and November, and the UK says earthquakes are a risk.

tips.text: Visa-free travelers must hold a confirmed return ticket, or an onward ticket and a visa for the next destination.

The Government of Canada and the UK FCDO say typhoons usually occur between May and November, with a risk of road blockages and landslides afterwards. The UK FCDO advises monitoring Central Weather Administration warnings and keeping your itinerary flexible.

Do not bring animal products into Taiwan without authorisation. The UK FCDO says you may face a heavy fine, and that customs have increased inspections because of African swine fever in pork products.

Submit the free online Taiwan Arrival Card through the National Immigration Agency's TWAC site, which says to complete it within 7 days before arrival. The UK and Canadian travel advice say within 3 days, so filing in the last 3 days satisfies both.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Taiwan?
faq.answer: 65 nationalities do not: the EU, UK, US, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and others get 90 days visa-free; Singapore, Malaysia, the Dominican Republic, Belize, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines get 30 days; and Thailand, the Philippines, Brunei and Oman get 14 days. 20 nationalities, including the Gulf states, can apply online for an eVisa, and citizens of India, Indonesia, Laos, Myanmar and Vietnam can apply online for a Travel Authorization Certificate. Everyone else applies for a visitor visa at a Taiwan overseas mission.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Taiwan?
faq.answer: US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 90 days with a confirmed return or onward ticket. The stay starts the day after arrival and cannot be extended.

faq.question: Can mainland Chinese citizens visit Taiwan?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states the entry rules for mainland Chinese citizens.

faq.question: Do Hong Kong and Macao residents need a visa for Taiwan?
faq.answer: Not a visa — Hong Kong and Macao residents can apply online to Taiwan's National Immigration Agency for an entry permit.

faq.question: Do I need an onward ticket to enter Taiwan visa-free?
faq.answer: Yes. BOCA lists a confirmed return ticket, or an onward ticket and a visa for the next destination, among the conditions of visa-free entry.
